The Graduate College
International Graduate Applicants
North Carolina A&T State University welcomes applications from international students. Admission to a graduate program requires both a departmental evaluation and final review by The Graduate College. Applicants must submit all required materials through the online application portal.
Access the Graduate Admissions Application Portal
Application Requirements
All international applicants must submit the following:
Completed online application
Application fee ($60, non-refundable)
Unofficial transcripts/mark sheets from all institutions attended
Personal statement (as required by program)
Three letters of recommendation
Graduate test scores (GRE/GMAT), if required by the program
English language proficiency documentation (if applicable)
Additional program-specific requirements (e.g., interviews) may apply. Meeting minimum requirements does not guarantee admission.
Transcript Evaluation Requirements
Applicants with academic records from institutions outside of the United States must:
Provide an official English translation of transcripts/mark sheets
Submit a course-by-course credential evaluation from one of the following agencies:
The Evaluation Company (SpanTran), WES, or ECE
The credential evaluation must be sent directly from the evaluation agency to The Graduate College.
English Language Proficiency
International applicants must demonstrate English proficiency through one of the following:
TOEFL (minimum score: 80 internet-based)
IELTS (minimum score: 6.0)
PTE Academic (minimum score: 75)
Duolingo English Test (minimum score: 115)
Scores must be sent directly from the testing agency and must be within two years of the test date.
Alternative Pathway:
Completion of Level 5 at Interlink Language Center or American Language Academy
Completion of a program from a CEA-accredited language academy
Exemptions may apply if the applicant:
Has earned a degree from an institution in a country where English is the official language of instruction
Has completed a degree at a U.S. institution
Is a native English speaker
Has resided legally in the U.S. for five or more years
International Applicant Deadlines
Fall Admission: May 15
General Deadlines:
November 1 (all admissions)
September 15 (spring admission)
Applicants are strongly encouraged to apply well in advance to allow time for visa processing, I-20 issuance, and travel planning.
After Admission: Final Review Requirements
If admitted, international applicants must submit the following before enrollment:
Official transcripts sent directly from issuing institutions
Official test scores (if required)
Official English proficiency scores (if applicable)
Verification of financial support for the duration of study
Current visa status documentation
Failure to submit required official documentation prior to enrollment may result in rescission of admission.
Visa and I-20 Processing
International applicants must work with the Office of International Affairs to obtain immigration documents.
For assistance, contact:
Office of International Affairs
122 Murphy Hall
Phone: (336) 334-7551
Applicants should allow sufficient time for visa processing and travel arrangements.
Important Notes for International Applicants
All application materials must be submitted electronically unless otherwise requested
Official documents must be sent directly from the issuing institution or agency
Documents submitted to the Graduate College are not returned
Applications may be deferred for up to one year with Graduate College approval
